question: Can the official LFM2.5-2.6B Q4_K_M GGUF execute through a bounded llama.cpp CPU route on the authorized Galaxy S23 Ultra under the canonical fixed-prompt contract?

scope.included: Text-only native reasoning continuation through the official LiquidAI GGUF and llama.cpp CPU.
excluded: GPU, NPU, HTP, or proprietary accelerator execution
host observations in the Android registry

canonical_protocol.request_isolation_strategy_pending_reaso: The bound llama-completion executable is for the first bounded Android viability smoke only. Before a canonical campaign, bind a loaded-route runner and prove one allowed isolation strategy; a per-process llama-completion loop is forbidden because it reloads the model.

upstream_model.name: LiquidAI/LFM2.5-2.6B
upstream_model.revision_proof: The deployed GGUF general.name is Ab00687315Bc1298E9D54E9C4B611Dde9867Ccc2; pinned upstream files at the normalized revision independently match the embedded tokenizer/template metadata.
upstream_model.architecture: LFM2, 30 layers, hidden size 2048, vocabulary size 128000

quantization.name: Q4_K_M
quantization.block_scheme: GGML K-quant medium. Q4_K uses 256-weight super-blocks; the M policy retains selected tensors at Q6_K and non-quantized metadata tensors at F32.
quantization.calibration_missing_reason: The official pinned repository and GGUF publish no importance-matrix or calibration provenance for this standard Q4_K_M artifact.
quantization.conversion_tool: llama.cpp GGUF conversion/quantization is implied by the official repository format and README
quantization.conversion_tool_revision_missing_reason: The official pinned repository and embedded GGUF metadata do not publish the exact converter/quantizer commit. Artifact bytes remain bound by repository revision, addition commit, size, and SHA-256.

tokenizer_and_template.tokenizer_type: embedded GGUF GPT-2/BPE with lfm2 pre-tokenizer
tokenizer_and_template.template_proof: Pinned upstream chat_template.jinja is byte-identical to tokenizer.chat_template embedded in the GGUF. tools/render_workloads.py is the exact no-tools, system+user, add_generation_prompt=true specialization.
tokenizer_and_template.bos_handling: The renderer emits <|startoftext|>; runtime tokenization must set tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token=false to prevent a second BOS.
tokenizer_and_template.reasoning: The model-native generation prompt ends with <think>; the route intentionally preserves the native reasoning continuation.
tokenizer_and_template.token_id_hash_encoding: Signed 32-bit token IDs serialized consecutively in little-endian order with no header.

runtime.name: llama.cpp
runtime.bounding: External 1800-second timeout plus a 16 MiB stdout file-size limit; raw partial output and stderr must be retained on timeout/error.
runtime.binary_scope: Bounded one-request Android viability smoke only. It must not be looped as a canonical campaign because each process reloads/remaps the model. A separately bound loaded-route runner and proven protocol-v2 isolation strategy are required before the 1+5+5+5 campaign.

android_build.reproducibility_flags: ffile-prefix-map for source and build roots; GGML_CCACHE=OFF; final binary stripped with the pinned NDK llvm-strip

device.phone_lock: artifacts/locks/phone.lock must be held across identity, staging, execution, evidence capture, and verified cleanup
device.phone_work_status: Not authorized for this continuation until Pi coordinates phone priority.
